text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Four leading members of the ruling Socialist Party's reformist wing said they were leaving the party and backed opposition's demands for immediate general elections.

-- Outgoing prime minister Zhan Videnov said that Bulgaria faced complete economic collapse unless the ruling Socialists and the opposition agreed urgently on forming a new cabinet to negotiate with international lenders. @

-- Outgoing finance minister Dimitar Kostov told the parliament's budget committee that the Bulgarian lev should be pegged to the German mark under a planned currency board system to facilitate Bulgaria's trade with other European countries.

-- A tougher version of a fixed exchange rate regime is more appropriate for Bulgaria because its economy and financial system are almost destroyed, International Monetary Fund resident representative Franek Rozwadowski said.
-- The Socialist parliamentary group discussed a draft programme for subsidising bread prices and freezing energy prices during during winter months.

-- The central bank paved the way for a restrictive fixed exchange rate regime by deciding to stop its open market operations through daily reverse repo-auctions held so far to regulate banks' liquidity. From Monday the Finance Ministry will issue daily seven-day T-bills to drain excessive liquidity.

-- Coins of 1, 2, 5 and 10 lev-denomination might soon disappear because their par value has fallen far below the price of the metal they are made from, making them a lucrative item for scrap metal traders, experts said. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
